Megan — thanks for the template and the clear asks. Below is a concise MAP proposal and our sizing recommendation based on your 25 qps / 2k token peak.

High-level recommendations (pilot -> production):
- Pilot (4 weeks): 4 x H100 (80GB) dedicated nodes — target latency 80–140ms depending on sequence distribution. Pilot validates prefix caching, batch sizes, and KV hit rates.
- Production ramp (Q1 after pilot): scale to 12–16 x H100 (shard across 2 availability zones) for sustained 25 qps with headroom and burst capacity. If H100 supply constrained, fallback: 8–12 x A100-80GB with tuned batching and slightly higher P99.

Lead-time estimates (calendar):
- Redwood Dedicated (reserved tranche, hosted): 4–6 weeks to provision committed capacity once PO is approved; additional 1–2 weeks for network/VPC peering and routing if needed.
- Redwood Private (customer-managed or on-prem): 10–14 weeks typical (vendor procurement + rack/cabling + on-site validation); if cloud partner marketplace order, ~8–10 weeks.

MAP skeleton (milestones & owners):
1) Sign SOW & PO — Owner: Marissa Cole — target: 2 weeks from now — deliverable: signed SOW + PO (sow_draft_v1.docx)
2) SOC2 & compliance review — Owner: Laura Bennett — target: +1 week after SOW — deliverable: security checklist, evidence bundle
3) Dedicated capacity reservation (if chosen) — Owner: Irene Choi / Redwood Ops — target: 4–6 weeks after PO — deliverable: reserved capacity confirmation
4) Private/on-prem procurement & install — Owner: Medica procurement / Redwood partner ops — target: 10–14 weeks — deliverable: rack-ready GPU nodes
5) Network & peering configuration — Owner: Medica cloud infra / Laura Bennett (info) — target: concurrent with provisioning — deliverable: peering test report
6) Acceptance tests & smoke run — Owner: Karthik Iyer — target: during pilot week 3 — deliverable: perf report, regression tests, token cost baseline
7) Go-live & scale plan — Owner: Megan / Irene — target: after acceptance — deliverable: scale runbook, rollback plan

Acceptance criteria suggestions:
- P99 latency < 200ms for 2k tokens on pilot hardware (measured over a 24h window)
- Model output quality baseline agreement on 100 sample prompts (file in Drive)
- KV cache hit rate > 40% for typical traffic (where applicable)
- Cost per 1k tokens within agreed band (TBD)

Related links: I've put a MAP draft into the shared Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2B3C-Medica-MAP and linked the HubSpot opportunity (see HubSpot link below). I'm attaching a SOW draft and will follow up with Marissa on pricing.

Next steps: Marissa will open the SOW + PO thread; Karthik will add technical acceptance test items; Laura will lead security evidence. If procurement wants a tighter calendar for Dedicated only, we can compress to 3–4 weeks with a committed deposit.

Best,
Irene Choi
Head of Customer Solutions — Redwood Inference

On Fri, Aug 15, 2025 at 1:45 PM Irene Choi <irene.ch@redwood.com> wrote:
> (Irene's MAP proposal)

Couple of technical notes to help procurement and infra decide on GPU mix and acceptance tests:

- Sequence length & KV cache: your 2k token average has a big impact on memory/KV working set. If you can provide a short token histogram (p0/p50/p90/p99) we can refine the exact node counts.
- Kernel selection: H100 gives better single-token throughput for long sequences; A100 is cost-effective for batched shorter sequences. We recommend H100 for initial latency-sensitive features, then add A100s for background / non-critical loads.
- Batching & quantization guidance: run in float16 with mixed-kernel path; enable 4-bit quantization for non-critical models to reduce memory footprint but validate quality on the 100-sample prompt set.
- Fallback plan: if H100 procurement slips, we can stage with 8 x A100-80GB with adjusted batch sizes and a temporary model shard strategy. Expect ~15–25% higher cost per token at this approach due to less efficient KV caching.

I attached a short note on kernel selection and expected memory numbers for 2k sequences: kernel_selection_notes.pdf.

I'll prepare the acceptance test checklist (perf, correctness, cost) and share it as a single-page runbook. Planning note: during pilot we will enable prefix caching and a small KV warmup window to reduce initial cold-starts.

—Karthik
Senior Solutions Architect — Redwood Inference
